anchor.statement: Proposition 9.1. Fix a label, m ∈ Z \ {0}, and α ∈ R . Let f m ∈ W α satisfy the support and smooth- extension hypotheses of Proposition 7.2. Assume also that the source harmonic f m e ikm Φ extends smoothly by zero outside the fixed local rectangle, including its pulse endpoints. Let (t m , π m ) be the solution of L m (t m , π m ) = − f m . The same conclusions hold for a homogeneous pulse t m ∈ W α , with f m = 0. Multiply its potential and pressure by the pulse cutoff and take the curl as in (7.38). Then the normalized linear residual, after adding the prescribed source f m e ikm Φ , belongs to W α +1/2−3 κs , apart from additive pulse-cutoff tails whose Cartesian space–time derivatives vanish to infinite order as q ↓ 0. The pressure amplitude π m belongs to W α +1/2 .

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: For the constructed inverse coefficients (input bounds assumed only for zero amplitudes), constructed_modal_particular_wave concludes amplitude in W^α, pressure in W^(α+1/2), good part in W^(α+1/2−3κ) and the exact identity residual + source = (good part + excluded-slot error)·carrier, and its _with_flat_error companion, for the same coefficients with the slot cutoff, states that the error lies in every unweighted class. Physical flatness of the error times the carrier needs excludedSlotError_carrier_physical_bound (not cited by the reviewer), and the homogeneous case is the linear theorem with source 0, where amplitude and pressure classes are hypotheses (InputBounds); the reviewer's 'primary pulse bounds' that would supply the pressure class are not cited.
